considerations.text: CLEARING THE FLOOR AREA IS THE EASY PART. The Class 3A route also demands a REAR location, services LINKED to the main house, and 14 days' notice — and the provision EXPIRES ON 31 DECEMBER 2030, so it is a window, not a permanent right. A SIDE-GARDEN SITE OR AN INDEPENDENT CONNECTION WOULD PUT THE PROJECT BACK INTO FULL PLANNING at any size. SECOND, this is a dwelling: Building Regulations, drainage and services apply as they would to a house extension. THIRD, no height, U-value, warranty or price is published, so thermal performance and cover cannot be compared with other suppliers. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm siting and services with the planning authority before ordering.

SITTING EXACTLY ON A STATUTORY CEILING IS A RISK IN ITSELF. The Class 3A maximum is 45 m2 and this product is 45.00 m2 — so any as-built variation upward, any measurement convention that includes wall thickness differently, or any addition such as a porch could take it outside the provision and into full planning. THE CERTIFIED LAYERS DO NOT PUBLISH WHICH MEASUREMENT BASIS THE 45 m2 REFERS TO, which is precisely the question that matters at the limit. SECOND, the rear-siting, linked-services and 14-day-notice conditions apply, and the provision expires 31 December 2030. THIRD, no height, U-value, warranty or price is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the measurement basis and the as-built area confirmed in writing before proceeding.

THREE SQUARE METRES CHANGE THE ENTIRE PROCESS. Above the 45 m2 Class 3A ceiling there is no notice route, no 14-day path and no exemption: a full planning application is required, with the fees, drawings, timeline and refusal risk that involves — and the 45 m2 model in the same range avoids all of it for 3 m2 less. SECOND, a dwelling of this size brings Building Regulations, drainage, services and likely a fire and access assessment. THIRD, no height, U-value, warranty or price is published, so nothing about the build quality can be compared. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: be certain the extra 3 m2 is worth a full application before choosing this over the 45 m2 unit.

THE PLANNING CONSEQUENCE IS THE SAME AS FOR ANY GARDEN BUILDING AND IS EASILY OVERLOOKED: the footprint of a sauna cabin counts toward the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance in full, so it reduces what remains for a future office, shed or studio. Neither the footprint nor the height is published, so neither statutory test could be run in the certified AM-006 layer. SECOND, THE TWO-MODEL PROBLEM: Aurea and Quu carry identical evidence positions, so a homeowner cannot rank them, and any comparison presented between them would be empty. Recorded once as a catalogue limitation; not corrected, architecture frozen. THIRD, PRACTICAL SAUNA-SPECIFIC POINTS THAT ATLAS CANNOT ANSWER: electrical supply for the heater, ventilation, and the base — all matter more for a sauna than for a dry office and none is held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat the electrical and base requirements as part of the price, and get the footprint in writing.

THE POINT BUYERS ROUTINELY MISS: AN OUTDOOR SAUNA IS A GARDEN STRUCTURE FOR PLANNING PURPOSES. The certified AM-006 layer records that a sauna cabin counts toward the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance alongside any shed, garage or garden room already on the plot — so its area matters even though the building is small. A sauna bought as a wellness purchase rather than a building purchase is exactly the kind of structure that quietly consumes the allowance a homeowner was saving for an office. SECOND, NEITHER STATUTORY TEST CAN BE RUN: no footprint and no height are published, so the 30 m2 allowance and the 3 m / 4 m height limits are both untestable. THIRD, THE CATEGORY PLACEMENT: held under Garden Rooms because Atlas has no correct category; recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. FOURTH, no price, warranty or installation scope is held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: add the sauna to your running total of garden structures before planning anything else.

THE RECORD IS TOO GENERAL TO SUPPORT ANY TEST. The certified AM-006 layer could not run the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance against it because no footprint is published, and it could not test the height condition either — 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m only for a tiled or slated pitched roof — because no height is published. Neither statutory test can be run. A SECOND, QUIETER ISSUE: a single catalogue entry standing for a supplier's whole garden-room offering cannot be compared on size, price or specification against the products in this Atlas that carry real figures, and any ranking that included it would flatter or penalise it arbitrarily. It should not appear in a size or value comparison in its present state. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the model list and a dimensioned plan; only then is a planning check or a price comparison meaningful.

A CURVED OR DOMED FORM RAISES THE HEIGHT QUESTION BEFORE THE AREA ONE. The 3 m limit applies to a flat or non-tiled roof and is measured to the highest point above finished ground level, so a rounded profile can approach it on a modest footprint — and no height is published. SECOND, NO VERIFIED FLOOR AREA EXISTS, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested either. THIRD, JURISDICTION: Northern Ireland has its own permitted development rules and supplier guidance from that jurisdiction must not be read across to a Republic site. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the external footprint, the overall height above ground level, and which jurisdiction's rules apply, before assuming any exemption.

TWO OBSTACLES SIT IN FRONT OF THIS PRODUCT, AND NEITHER IS ABOUT SIZE. FIRST, JURISDICTION: Northern Ireland has its own permitted development rules, so any planning guidance the supplier gives from its own jurisdiction MUST NOT BE READ ACROSS to a Republic site — and the 30 m2 allowance, the 3 m and 4 m height limits and the 25 m2 open-space condition govern only the Republic. SECOND, USE: overnight occupation removes the Class 3 exemption whatever the area turns out to be. THIRD, no verified floor area exists, so even the Class 3A band cannot be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the floor area AND which jurisdiction's rules apply to your site before assuming any exemption.

SMALL DOES NOT MEAN EXEMPT, AND THIS PRODUCT IS THE CLEAREST ILLUSTRATION IN THE CATALOGUE. Sleeping use removes the Class 3 exemption at any size, so a hut of 10 m2 used as a guest bedroom is in a worse position than a 24 m2 office used as an office. SECOND, JURISDICTION: Berko is Northern Ireland based, where the Irish regime does not apply, so supplier guidance from its own jurisdiction must not be read across to a Republic site. THIRD, no verified floor area or height exists, so neither the 30 m2 allowance nor the 3 m and 4 m limits can be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm floor area, INTENDED USE and applicable jurisdiction — in that order of consequence, use first.

NOTHING ABOUT THIS RECORD CAN BE COMPARED, AND THAT CUTS AGAINST THE BUYER AS WELL AS FOR THEM. With no fixed area, no price, no specification and no product URL, the record cannot be ranked against catalogue products on size, cost per square metre or thermal performance, and it cannot be tested against either statutory condition in advance — the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m / 4 m height limits both apply to whatever is finally built. SECOND, A SUPPLIER-LEVEL RECORD DEFECT carried from the certified layers: this organisation's name, 'Garden Rooms', is also the Atlas Product Category name, which makes attribution ambiguous wherever category and supplier appear together. Recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. THIRD, ON A BESPOKE PROJECT EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS IS IN THE QUOTATION — there is no catalogue to fall back on if the specification is thin. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: insist the quotation states the external footprint, the finished height and the wall build-up.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, CHANGE OF USE IS THE HARDER QUESTION AND IT SITS BEHIND THE AREA ONE: a treatment room implies CLIENTS VISITING THE PROPERTY, and COMMERCIAL USE IS NOT INCIDENTAL USE. The Class 3 exemption requires the building to remain incidental to the enjoyment of the house. Nothing has been assumed here about how the buyer intends to run it — but the exemption cannot be relied on without settling it. TWO, NO AREA IS PUBLISHED: the certified AM-001 layer holds no floor area and no dimensions and records that 'DELUXE' IS A SPECIFICATION LABEL, NOT A SIZE. Nothing estimated. DO NOT RANK. The area test cannot be run. THREE, HEATING AND ACOUSTICS ARE BOTH UNPUBLISHED AND BOTH MATTER HERE: the certified thermal record notes the envelope supports a steady temperature for a client lying still, but THE HEATING SPECIFICATION IS NOT PUBLISHED and must be established separately; and the certified insulation record notes treatment-room use implies ACOUSTIC PRIVACY with NO ACOUSTIC SPECIFICATION PUBLISHED. FOUR, CRANE ACCESS is the gating physical constraint and THE BASE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED — a settlement defect would fall outside the building guarantee. FIVE, WARRANTY DETAIL: twenty years is published without scope, exclusions or transferability, and it is not confirmed the term reaches this configuration rather than only the residential tiny homes the phrase names. No SIPS thickness or U-value; no delivery radius published.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PLANNING, AND IT OUTRANKS EVERYTHING ELSE: the fit-out decides this product. Bathroom plus kitchenette equals equipped for habitation; Class 3 requires incidental use and NO HUMAN HABITATION; so this is unlikely to qualify as an exempt garden structure at ANY area. The Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route runs 32-45 m2 with rear siting, linked services and 14 days' notice, and EXPIRES 31 DECEMBER 2030 — and because it has a 32 m2 FLOOR, a smaller unit falls BETWEEN THE TWO ROUTES and needs full permission. TWO, NO AREA IS PUBLISHED, so neither route can even be tested — the certified AM-001 layer holds no floor area and no dimensions and estimates nothing. DO NOT RANK. THREE, SERVICES: a bathroom and kitchenette imply water and drainage connections carrying Irish planning and BUILDING-REGULATION implications separate from thermal performance, none of it verified. Establish who makes the connections and to what standard. FOUR, WARRANTY BOUNDARIES: twenty years is published without scope or conditions, and FITTED SANITARYWARE AND APPLIANCES usually carry their own manufacturer terms rather than the building guarantee — ask which applies to what. FIVE, COST AND ACCESS: press coverage reports a 25 m2 unit with bathroom and kitchenette at EUR 60,000-70,000, well above the garden-office suppliers in this catalogue and reflecting a residential-grade fitted product; units are craned, so crane access is the gating physical constraint; and the base position is unresolved.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, NO AREA IS PUBLISHED AT ALL: the certified AM-001 layer holds no floor area, no dimensions and NO DERIVABLE FOOTPRINT, and nothing has been estimated. DO NOT RANK on any basis. The planning area test cannot be run. AND THE INTEGRAL STORAGE COUNTS — storage built into the unit falls inside the same 30 m2 combined allowance as the office, so the figure you need is the TOTAL external footprint, office and store together. Ask for it in writing before assuming exemption. TWO, CRANE ACCESS IS THE GATING PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT: units are craned onto site (press-reported, not supplier-published). A crane needs a route and a standing position, and a site that cannot take one cannot take this product. THREE, THE BASE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED: the supplier publishes that it installs, but not what the installation includes underneath — and a settlement defect would then sit outside the building guarantee. FOUR, THE WARRANTY IS LENGTH WITHOUT DETAIL: twenty years is published; scope, exclusions, claims procedure and transferability are not, nor is it confirmed that the term extends to the home-office configurations rather than only to the residential tiny homes the published phrase names. FIVE, THERMAL AND PRICE: no SIPS panel thickness and no U-value published; the 'A BER rating' claim rates whole DWELLINGS on energy use, not garden buildings on fabric, so it is not the wall U-value a garden-office buyer needs. No delivery radius is published from Bandon.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, NO AREA PUBLISHED: the certified AM-001 layer holds no floor area and no dimensions, and records explicitly that 'MULTI USE' DESCRIBES FLEXIBILITY OF USE, NOT A SIZE, and has not been treated as a measurement. Nothing estimated. DO NOT RANK. The planning area test cannot be run at all. TWO, THE USE CONDITION IS THE LIVE ONE ON THIS MODEL: flexibility is the selling point, and the exemption holds only while the building remains INCIDENTAL to the house and is NOT USED FOR HUMAN HABITATION. A use that is fine today can take the building outside the exemption tomorrow without anything physical changing. Be specific with the planning authority about which use you intend. THREE, CRANE ACCESS IS THE GATING PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT — units are craned onto site (press-reported), and a site that cannot take a crane cannot take this product. FOUR, THE BASE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED: the supplier publishes that it installs, not what sits underneath, so a settlement defect would fall outside the building guarantee. FIVE, WARRANTY AND THERMAL DETAIL: twenty years is published without scope, exclusions, claims procedure or transferability, and it is not confirmed that the term applies to this configuration rather than only to the residential tiny homes the phrase names; no SIPS panel thickness or U-value is published; and the 'A BER rating' is a whole-dwelling energy rating, not a fabric figure. No delivery radius is published from Bandon.

A PRODUCT PAGE THAT RETURNS NO SPECIFICATION ON REPEATED ATTEMPTS, WHERE EVERY SIBLING PAGE RETURNS ONE FIRST TIME, IS A SIGNAL IN ITSELF — the model may be withdrawn. SECOND, EVEN THE WALL THICKNESS IS UNREAD for this model, and within this range that matters enormously: 19 mm and 92 mm are very different buildings, and the certified layer says so directly. THIRD, whatever the thickness, it is UNINSULATED — Lasita's optional Complete Insulation Kit covers FLOOR AND ROOF ONLY, with no wall option anywhere in the catalogue. FOURTH, DIY kit only, base excluded, Republic of Ireland unconfirmed, warranty 2 or 5 years unstated per model. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the model exists and get the wall thickness on any quotation.

THE ROOF ARRIVES BARE, AND THAT IS THE MOST URGENT POINT — the supplier's own guidance is that bare roof boards will not keep the structure dry, with bitumen shingles or metal roofing offered as PAID OPTIONS. SECOND, IT IS UNINSULATED: insulation is a separately priced extra at EUR 1,900 for floor and roof in 50 mm PIR, EUR 2,640 for 100 mm Rockwool, and EUR 4,400 for wall insulation. TOGETHER A ROOF COVERING AND INSULATION CAN ADD MORE THAN EUR 6,000 TO A EUR 6,171 HEADLINE PRICE. THIRD, A SUPPLIER DATA DEFECT is recorded, not corrected: the technical table gives 'Ridge height: 249 mm', which cannot be right against 210 cm eaves — a unit error for 249 cm. FOURTH, NAMING INTEGRITY: the page body, image and configurable option all call this model 'Davos 44 A'. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the real cost is roughly double the headline.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, A BESPOKE ROUTE TRANSFERS THE SPECIFICATION BURDEN TO YOU. Nothing is fixed, which means nothing is guaranteed unless you write it down: insulation build-up, internal height, electrical schedule, floor construction, glazing specification and base provision are all design-stage decisions with no published default. An informed buyer can get a better building here than from any catalogue; an uninformed one has nothing to hold the supplier to. TWO, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED — a '10-Year aftercare warranty' and a '10-month aftercare warranty' are both published on the same page, the shorter repeated in the FAQ. A factor of twelve. Get the document before deposit. THREE, NO PRICE IS PUBLISHED for any garden room; the store carries cladding, tiles and decking only. No comparison is possible before quotation. FOUR, THE BASE POSITION IS NOT PUBLISHED, and a recorded internal inconsistency stands between 'built on site from start to finish' and separately marketed 'modular garden rooms' made in sections. FIVE, CROSS-BORDER TERMS ARE ABSENT: nothing is published on VAT treatment, contract currency or governing jurisdiction, all of which matter on a Northern Ireland to Republic purchase. No area or dimensions: DO NOT RANK.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL ITEM: the supplier publishes BOTH a '10-Year aftercare warranty' and a '10-month aftercare warranty' on the same page, the shorter figure repeated in its own FAQ. A factor of twelve separates a market-leading term from one below every published warranty in this Atlas. Get the document before deposit. TWO, NO AREA, NO DIMENSIONS AND NO PRICE ARE PUBLISHED for any garden room — the store carries cladding, tiles and decking only. Nothing can be compared against another supplier until you have a quotation. DO NOT RANK. THREE, THE BASE POSITION IS NOT PUBLISHED: the supplier builds on site but does not state whether groundworks sit inside the quoted price. FOUR, NO INSULATION MATERIAL, THICKNESS OR U-VALUE is published — the envelope is established as genuinely insulated and cannot be quantified or ranked against Pineca Ireland's published U-values or SIPS-House's 0.031 W/mK. FIVE, PLANNING AND USE: the 30 m2 combined allowance requires INCIDENTAL use and NO HUMAN HABITATION, so this room may be lived in during the day but not slept in. Cross-border buyers should also note that VAT treatment, contract currency and governing jurisdiction are nowhere published.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE GYM-SPECIFIC. ONE, THE FLOOR AND THE BASE ARE BOTH UNPUBLISHED. A gym floor takes dynamic load from dropped weights and machines, and the supplier states neither the floor construction nor whether the groundworks beneath the building are inside the price. Those two questions decide whether the building survives the use. TWO, NO INTERNAL CLEAR HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, and the exemption caps EXTERNAL height at 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof — so overhead training has to be designed into a 3 m envelope deliberately. THREE, THE NOISE-REDUCTION CLAIM IS UNQUANTIFIED. The product is sold partly on reducing noise and no acoustic specification of any kind is published; if neighbours are close, that claim cannot be relied on as published. FOUR, MOISTURE: exercise puts significant water vapour into a sealed room, and no vapour-control or ventilation detail is published. FIVE, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED between ten years and ten months, and on a gym the scope question compounds it — ask specifically whether the floor structure and the base are covered. No area, dimensions or price are published: DO NOT RANK.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE CONTESTED WARRANTY MATTERS MOST ON AN OFFICE: the supplier publishes both a '10-Year aftercare warranty' and a '10-month aftercare warranty' on the same page. The defects that surface between year two and year five — glazing seals, roof membrane, condensation, door alignment — fall comfortably inside a ten-year term and far outside a ten-month one. This is a building your income depends on; get the document before deposit. TWO, NO AREA AND NO PRICE ARE PUBLISHED. Nothing here can be compared against a competitor until you hold a quotation, and no cost per square metre can be calculated. DO NOT RANK. THREE, NO ELECTRICAL SPECIFICATION IS PUBLISHED — sockets, lighting and data provision are nowhere stated, and for an office a hard network point and adequate socket count are basic requirements. Ask for the electrical schedule. FOUR, NO INSULATION THICKNESS OR U-VALUE, so running cost cannot be estimated. FIVE, THE BASE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED, and a recorded internal inconsistency stands: the supplier publishes both 'built on site from start to finish' and a description of modular rooms 'made in sections'. Confirm which route your quotation covers.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, CHANGE OF USE OUTRANKS EVERYTHING ELSE HERE. The product is published for running a business from home, and CLIENTS VISITING THE PROPERTY IS NOT INCIDENTAL USE — the 30 m2 back-garden exemption requires the building to remain incidental to the enjoyment of the house. Take planning advice before ordering; Atlas makes no determination. TWO, PLUMBING IS NOT ADDRESSED. Nothing published confirms the supplier provides a sink, wash station or WC, and most salon and therapy uses need at least one. Raise it at design stage rather than assuming it. THREE, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED between ten years and ten months — and on a revenue-generating asset, a defect that closes the room closes the business with it. A ten-month term expires before the second winter. FOUR, CROSS-BORDER COMMERCIAL EXPOSURE: for a Republic buyer, VAT registration, Irish insurance and Irish change-of-use all apply, and a Northern Ireland contractor's quotation addresses none of them. Nothing is published on VAT treatment, contract currency or governing jurisdiction. FIVE, NO AREA, NO WALL LENGTH, NO CLEAR HEIGHT AND NO PRICE are published. DO NOT RANK.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE SOUND-CONTROL CLAIM IS THE PRODUCT'S CENTRAL PROMISE AND IT IS ENTIRELY UNQUANTIFIED. No acoustic specification, no sound-reduction figure and no supporting construction detail is published anywhere. For a room bought largely on acoustic calm, that is the gap that matters most — ask what it consists of in materials and construction before ordering. TWO, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED between ten years and ten months. A sensory room is usually provided for an ongoing need expected to last years; a ten-month term would expire inside the first period of use it is bought for. THREE, NO THERMAL SPECIFICATION: no insulation material, thickness or U-value, so temperature stability — which matters for sensory regulation — cannot be assessed from published evidence. FOUR, NO AREA, DIMENSIONS OR PRICE are published, so nothing here can be compared against another route until you hold a quotation. DO NOT RANK. FIVE, PLANNING: the room must remain incidental to the house and must not be slept in; the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m / 4 m height limits apply, and the footprint is yours to set at design stage.

NEITHER STATUTORY TEST CAN BE RUN AND NO COMPARISON IS POSSIBLE. With no footprint the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested, and with no height the 3 m limit for a flat or non-tiled roof — 4 m only for tiled or slated — cannot be checked either. Whatever is finally built will have to be tested on its own dimensions. SECOND, THE RANGE-LEVEL STRUCTURE IS A CATALOGUE DEFECT rather than a supplier failing: a record standing for a family of models cannot carry product-level decision intelligence and should not appear in a size, price or performance ranking in its present state. Recorded once; not corrected, architecture frozen. THIRD, THE ORGANISATION NAME 'Garden Rooms' duplicates the Atlas Product Category name, making supplier attribution ambiguous in any listing showing both. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this record identifies a family, not a purchase — get the model list before anything else.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, HEIGHT IS THE LIVE CONDITION FOR A GYM AND IT IS NOT PUBLISHED: internal clear height matters for overhead pressing, pull-up bars and skipping, and no certified layer holds it. The Irish exempted-development external limit is 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitch. TWO, ACOUSTICS: no acoustic specification is published, which the certified insulation layer records as directly relevant to gym use — dropped weights transmit to neighbours and there is no evidence on which to assess it. THREE, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. A gym floor takes dynamic load, so ask specifically whether the floor structure and the foundation are inside any guarantee offered at quotation; the UK same-name company's terms were deliberately not transferred. FOUR, MEASUREMENT: internal versus external is not stated and nothing has been deducted. DO NOT RANK on internal area. FIVE, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY, and the supplier's published planning guidance is UK law that does not apply in Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: area is comfortable here; height, acoustics and warranty are what to establish in writing.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY. Two show sites, Nottingham and Studley, nationwide UK delivery, no Irish premises, dealer or delivery statement. SAME-NAME TRAP, restated once because it is the most consequential fact about this supplier: cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are SEPARATE COMPANIES. Establish which one you are dealing with before paying a deposit. TWO, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. No warranty term, scope or claims procedure could be located for the Irish company; the UK same-name company's ten-year terms have deliberately NOT been transferred. The gap matters more here than elsewhere precisely because the supplier's scope is so broad — groundworks through to wiring is exactly what a warranty would need to cover. THREE, MEASUREMENT: internal versus external is not stated and nothing has been deducted. DO NOT RANK this product on internal area. FOUR, THERMAL: no insulation thickness and no U-value for any element, so the building is established as genuinely insulated but cannot be ranked numerically. FIVE, PLANNING: the supplier's published planning guidance is UK LAW — under 20 m2 and a 2.5 m height limit — and does not apply in Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the warranty and the internal clear height in writing.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PLANNING HEADROOM: at 18 m2 this unit consumes 60 per cent of the 30 m2 COMBINED back-garden allowance on its own. About 12 m2 remains for everything else on the plot — enough for a modest shed, not for a garage. If a structure is already there, check the plot total before ordering. TWO, THERMAL, AND IT MATTERS MOST HERE: no insulation thickness and no U-value are published for any element, and running cost scales with area — so this is the model in the range where the absence of a fabric figure has the largest financial consequence. THREE, HEIGHT: internal clear height is not published, and for gym use it is decision-critical; the Irish exempted-development limit is 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitch. FOUR, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. On the largest and most expensive building in the range there is no published cover on either the structure or the groundworks the supplier lays. FIVE, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY; cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are separate companies. MEASUREMENT: internal versus external unstated, DO NOT RANK on internal area.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE MOST IMPORTANT: at 5 m2 the certified AM-001 layer records that WALL BUILD-UP CONSUMES A HIGH PROPORTION OF THE FOOTPRINT, so usable internal space is MATERIALLY BELOW 5 m2. Internal versus external is not stated and nothing has been deducted. DO NOT RANK on internal area. At this scale that is not a technicality — it is the difference between a workable desk and an unusable one. TWO, COST PER SQUARE METRE: GBP 14,400 is a starting-from price and is only about GBP 1,150 below the 3.2 m x 2.3 m model, which offers roughly 47 per cent more area. Within this range price does not scale with size, so the smallest unit is by far the worst value per square metre. VAT treatment is not stated. THREE, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. The UK same-name company's terms were deliberately not transferred. FOUR, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY, priced in GBP; cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are separate companies. FIVE: the mains connection from the house needs a separately arranged electrician — a real cost outside the quoted price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: view one before ordering.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, COST PER SQUARE METRE: GBP 15,550 is a starting-from price for roughly 7.36 m2. Several rooms elsewhere in this Atlas offer double or triple the area for a comparable figure — though not all include the base and electrics. VAT treatment is not stated in the certified evidence. TWO, USABLE SPACE: the certified AM-001 layer records that at this size wall build-up consumes a high proportion of the footprint, so usable internal space is MATERIALLY BELOW 7.36 m2, and no subtraction has been made. Internal versus external is not stated. DO NOT RANK on internal area. THREE, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. No published term exists to weigh against competitors offering ten and twelve year cover. The UK same-name company's terms have deliberately not been transferred. FOUR, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY, priced in GBP. SAME-NAME TRAP: cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are separate companies. FIVE, THERMAL: no thickness and no U-value published for any element. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: sit in one at a show site before ordering — at this size the difference between adequate and cramped is a matter of centimetres.

GBP 15,100 is a starting-from price, not a fixed one, and at roughly 6m2 that is expensive per square metre — several rooms in this review offer double or triple the area for a similar figure. VAT treatment is not stated in the reviewed source. Insulation specification is not recorded in Atlas for this product, so year-round comfort cannot be assessed from the evidence held. Priced in GBP: Irish buyers should confirm delivery to Ireland and currency terms.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE DIMENSIONS THAT MATTER MOST ARE NOT PUBLISHED: internal clear height and usable wall length are decision-critical for studio work and neither is held in any certified layer. TWO, MEASUREMENT-IDENTICAL TO THE GARDEN GYM 5m x 3m: the certified AM-001 layer records that this product and the Garden Gym 5m x 3m share identical stated dimensions and are distinguished by intended use, not size — no size or price-per-square-metre comparison can separate them, and Atlas has not created one. THREE, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. No term, scope or claims procedure could be located for this supplier; the UK same-name company's ten-year terms were deliberately not transferred. FOUR, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY, show sites at Nottingham and Studley, no Irish route. SAME-NAME TRAP: cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are separate companies. FIVE, PLANNING: the supplier's own planning guidance is UK law and does not apply in Ireland; and any studio operated as a business must be checked against the INCIDENTAL USE condition, which is a live question for commercial photography, not a formality. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm height, wall length and use class before ordering.

EVEN THE ROOF IS DELIVERED WITHOUT A COVERING, so as supplied this is realistically a summer room rather than a three-season one. REACHING YEAR-ROUND USE MEANS BUYING THE INSULATION PACKAGES SEPARATELY, which on this model would add EUR 800 to EUR 4,730 to a EUR 4,870 headline price — A DOUBLING IN THE WORST CASE. Any comparison of this product's price against an insulated garden room is therefore NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE. SECOND, THE PUBLISHED EXTERNAL FIGURES DIFFER BY MORE THAN 3 m2, so the planning area test must not be run from the title dimension. THIRD, the '44' is a log profile in millimetres, not an area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get one confirmed external footprint and one all-in price before comparing anything.

THE HEADLINE AREA IS NOT A SINGLE ROOM, AND THE SPLIT IS NOT PUBLISHED — a homeowner planning a desk and a sofa into 15.96 m2 may find materially less. SECOND, A 'CARROZ 2' ALSO EXISTS AT THE SAME 15.96 m2, so a quotation should name the exact model; this record is matched to the base Carroz. THIRD, 28 mm walls with a floor-and-roof-only insulation option means a three-season building with no route to insulated walls through the supplier. FOURTH, DIY kit only, foundation the buyer's responsibility. FIFTH, Republic of Ireland unconfirmed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm which Carroz, and get the two room sizes separately.

The pricing does not reward you for choosing smaller: at EUR 32,950 this is EUR 1,950 dearer than the 19.1m² Cabin 19m² Studio and EUR 5,550 cheaper than the 26m² Studio — roughly EUR 1,938 per m², the second-worst value in the Concept Modular range. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: stand in a room this size before ordering one.

KNOWING THE LIMIT IS 3 m IS ONLY HALF THE TEST — THE OTHER HALF IS THE BUILDING'S ACTUAL HEIGHT, WHICH IS NOT PUBLISHED. NEITHER STATUTORY TEST CAN BE RUN, AND THE CERTIFIED RECORD SAYS SO IN THOSE WORDS: no published footprint and no published height. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the roofed footprint in metres and the height in writing, and count that footprint alongside any existing shed, garage or garden room.

AN EDITION NAME THAT IMPLIES A HIGHER SPECIFICATION WITHOUT PUBLISHING ONE IS THE PARTICULAR PROBLEM HERE. 'Superior' suggests more than the Legend or the Essential, but Atlas holds no figure that would confirm it — no size, no structure, no glazing, no price — so a buyer paying a premium is doing so on the strength of the word alone. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask exactly what 'Superior' delivers over the other editions, in specification terms, before accepting a price difference.

A COVER IS THE STRUCTURE MOST LIKELY TO EXHAUST AN ALLOWANCE UNNOTICED, and the certified record says so directly. Terrace covers are typically sized to the patio rather than to a room, so they are often LARGER in plan than a garden office — while feeling like an accessory rather than a building. Add an existing shed and the 30 m2 can be gone before any garden room is considered. SECOND, NOTHING MEASURABLE IS PUBLISHED: no covered footprint, no height. THIRD, no Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat the covered area as counting toward the combined 30 m2, get it in metres in writing, and total the garden before committing.

Until then it belongs on an enquiry list, not a shortlist.

THE PAGE DESCRIBES THIS MODEL AS 'DESIGNED FOR YEAR-ROUND USE' AND THE SPECIFICATION CONTAINS NO INSULATION AT ALL — the same conflict recorded on the Havana, and the certified layer classifies it UNINSULATED on the published build. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: 'home office' in the name and 'year-round' in the copy are marketing; ask for the wall, floor and roof build-up.

THE CERTIFIED RECORD IS BLUNT: THE TEST CANNOT BE RUN ON HELD DATA, AND THERE IS NO IRISH PURCHASING ROUTE. SEVEN MODELS THAT CANNOT BE TOLD APART IS A SHOPPING PROBLEM BEFORE IT IS A PLANNING ONE. With numerals that convey no area and Plus suffixes with no recorded content, a buyer has no basis on which to choose — and if the models do differ in footprint, their positions against the 30 m2 combined allowance differ with them. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping, which the certified layers note makes the area question moot for an Irish buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for a size table covering the whole line.

AN UNDEFINED UPGRADE ON AN UNDEFINED SIZE IS TWO UNKNOWNS MULTIPLIED. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so neither statutory test can be run. THIRD, Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor. IF THE NUMERALS DO TRACK SIZE, THIS IS WHERE THE ALLOWANCE STARTS TO MATTER — AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT CANNOT BE CHECKED. THE PLUS TIER IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE UNKNOWN IN THE RANGE. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping, which the certified record notes makes the area test moot for an Irish buyer in any case. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the Plus specification itemised before the price is agreed.

AVAILABILITY IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, AND THE CERTIFIED RECORD SAYS SO. IF A ROUTE WERE ESTABLISHED, the largest model in an undimensioned line would be the hardest to plan around: the 30 m2 is COMBINED across every garden structure, the pent roof caps height at 3 m, and neither figure is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: settle the route before the specification.

THE FLAGSHIP OF AN UNDIMENSIONED LINE IS WHERE THE MOST MONEY MEETS THE LEAST INFORMATION. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping, which makes all of the above moot for an Irish buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at the top of the range, insist on a dimensioned drawing and an itemised specification.

AN OFFICE LIVES OR DIES ON ITS ENVELOPE, AND NO ENVELOPE SPECIFICATION EXISTS. No U-value, wall build-up, glazing specification or heating provision is published for any Bertilo product, so whether this room is usable in January cannot be assessed — the single most consequential gap for a daily workspace. THIRD, A BUSINESS WITH VISITING CLIENTS may move beyond incidental domestic use, the caution the certified layers raise for the workshop models. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what the walls are made of before asking anything else.

A POOL SITE IS A CROWDED SITE, AND THE ALLOWANCE IS COMBINED. Pool plant housing, storage and often a terrace cover already occupy built area, so a poolhouse is frequently the addition that tips a garden past 30 m2 — and no audited area is held for this building with which to check. SECOND, THE CERTIFIED CAUTION STANDS: a poolhouse serving a pool may raise considerations beyond the garden-structure tests. THIRD, humidity is the defining interior condition and no ventilation specification is published. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: total every structure around the pool before adding another.

A LARGER OFFICE UNDER A PENT ROOF PUSHES AGAINST THE HEIGHT CAP AND THE AREA LIMIT AT THE SAME TIME. THE LARGEST BUILDING ON THE MOST DEVELOPED KIND OF SITE IS THE WORST COMBINATION FOR AN ALLOWANCE CHECK. A pool garden typically already carries plant housing, storage and often a cover, and the 30 m2 is COMBINED across all of it — with no audited area for this building and no height for the pent-roof cap. SECOND, THE POOLHOUSE CAUTION STANDS: a building serving a swimming pool may raise separate considerations. THIRD, humidity handling is unspecified. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping means no supplier on the ground. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: measure the whole site first, then ask for this building's external footprint in metres.

THE AMBIGUOUS NUMERAL IS THE CENTRAL PROBLEM AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. If 17 means 17 m2, the pod sits comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with room to spare; if 17 is a model number, the building could be any size at all, including one that exceeds the limit. A homeowner reading the name would naturally assume the first, and that assumption is unsupported. THIRD, NOTHING IS HELD ON CONSTRUCTION, WARRANTY, INSTALLATION OR PRICE, so the record cannot enter a value or comfort comparison. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint, the measurement basis and the ridge and eaves heights in writing before treating this as exempt.

THE USE EXCLUSION IS DECISIVE AND IT IS NOT ABOUT SIZE. Sleeping accommodation is outside the Class 3 exemption whatever the footprint, so a buyer cannot make this pod exempt by choosing a smaller one. THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTE HAS A FLOOR AS WELL AS A CEILING: Class 3A covers 32 to 45 m2, requires siting to the rear, services linked to the principal house, at least 14 days' written notice to the planning authority and Building and Fire Regulations compliance, and expires on 31 December 2030 — a materially more demanding process than buying a garden office. SECOND, THE SIZE IS UNKNOWN: the numeral 22 may be a model number, so the pod cannot even be placed relative to the 32 m2 Class 3A minimum. THIRD, NOTHING IS HELD ON SERVICES, INSULATION OR WARRANTY, and for a building someone will sleep in, those are not optional details. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a consent project before it is a purchase.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PRODUCT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED AND IT OUTRANKS THE REST: the certified thermal layer records that NO QC8 APPEARS IN THE SUPPLIER'S CURRENT PUBLISHED RANGE — its own FAQ names two offices plus the Annexe: the QCB5, the QC9 and the Annexe. This record cannot be matched to a live model and may be a superseded specification. Recorded, NOT corrected. Confirm the model name with the supplier before treating any figure here as a live quotation. TWO, STANDARD INTERNAL HEIGHT IS 2,080 mm, WHICH THE CERTIFIED LAYER RECORDS AS LOW FOR OVERHEAD LIFTING — the single most important number for a gym, and the reason the 7 ft 10 in extended-height option exists. Specify it deliberately; do not assume it. THREE, HEATING IS NOT INCLUDED in any Booths building: the recommended air-conditioning unit adds roughly GBP 1,700 to install plus a service every two years, or the buyer fits electric heaters. A headline price is not a heated building. FOUR, AVAILABILITY: free delivery and installation in ENGLAND, GBP 899 to Scotland within 100 miles of Edinburgh or Glasgow, NO IRISH DELIVERY PUBLISHED; Corby, Northamptonshire. And every planning claim on the site is UK law — permitted development at 2.5 m height — which does not apply in Ireland. FIVE, THERMAL AND MEASUREMENT: no U-value is published for any element, so the envelope cannot be ranked numerically against Dunster House's stated 0.7 W/m2K; an unreconciled inconsistency stands, 90 mm of wall insulation against a 75 mm panel thickness; and no area or dimensions are held. DO NOT RANK.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS HERE ARE THE ENVELOPE AND THE HEIGHT, NOT THE AREA. No U-value, wall build-up or insulation specification is published, so year-round usability cannot be assessed — and in a building of this size the difference between an insulated and an uninsulated shell decides whether it is usable in January or only in summer. NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED EITHER, so the 3 m flat-roof and 4 m tiled-pitched limits cannot be tested. THIRD, the imperial designation is a rounded trade convention rather than a measurement, though at 22 m2 of headroom that is immaterial. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the questions worth asking are about insulation and ridge height.

FOUR AND A HALF SQUARE METRES IS A BOOTH, NOT A ROOM. A desk, a chair and a narrow walkway is the realistic contents; there is no space for a second person, a printer table or storage, and anyone whose work involves materials or equipment will outgrow it immediately. THAT IS THE MAIN CONSIDERATION, AND IT IS PRACTICAL RATHER THAN REGULATORY. ON THE REGULATORY SIDE, the certified layers note the 6 × 8 ft figure is a rounded imperial nominal designation rather than a measured area — harmless at this scale. NO HEIGHT, U-VALUE OR INSULATION SPECIFICATION IS PUBLISHED, and in a very small building thermal performance is felt quickly. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: measure your desk and equipment before ordering, and ask what insulation is fitted.

GYM USE PUTS PRESSURE ON THE ONE DIMENSION THE EXEMPTION CAPS HARDEST. Standing exercise, a rack or a treadmill sets a minimum internal clear height; the floor build-up sits below it and the roof structure above; and the overall height above finished ground level is what the 3 m flat-roof limit measures. NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so it cannot be tested. SECOND, NO AREA IS PUBLISHED EITHER, and the certified layers are explicit that the sibling models' 6 × 8 ft figure has NOT been carried across. THIRD, nothing is held on floor loading or ventilation, both of which matter for the intended use. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for footprint, overall height, internal clear height and floor specification together, in writing.

THE NAME INVITES THE ONE USE THAT WOULD REMOVE THE EXEMPTION. A 'retreat' that becomes a spare bedroom for a weekend visitor is human habitation, and habitation is excluded from the Class 3 exemption at ANY floor area — so a 4.46 m2 building used for sleeping is in a worse regulatory position than a 24 m2 building used as an office. SECOND, THE SPECIFICATIONS ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE QCB5 OFFICE ON PUBLISHED EVIDENCE: same nominal size, no height, no insulation figure, no price, so nothing here justifies choosing between them on anything but the name. THIRD, no height is published for the 3 m and 4 m tests. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: decide the use honestly, and ask Booths what actually differs between the two models.

The large fixed window is the range's defining feature and also its main thermal compromise: Sanctum itself notes that 'the bigger the surface area of glazing the more potential heat loss', and the windows carry the weakest published U-value in its specification at approximately 1.7 against 0.2-0.3 for the opaque envelope. A fixed window also cannot be opened for ventilation. No U-value table is published for the QuadPod range specifically — the figures Atlas holds come from the Urban Composite page. Atlas holds no size-specific price for this variant, only the GBP 10,995 range entry price. Internal dimensions are 0.15m under the nominal name on each axis. IRISH BUYERS: UK supplier, GBP pricing, no published route to the Republic of Ireland.

From GBP 10,995 this is the least floor space per pound in the Sanctum range — a smaller building than the Hampton 2.4m x 2.4m at roughly GBP 2,000 more. Internal dimensions are 0.15m under the nominal on each axis, which is proportionally severe at this size: verify the internal figure before assuming a desk and chair will fit comfortably. The U-values Atlas holds against this product are published on the Urban Composite page, not for the QuadPod range, and are labelled 'Approx' by the supplier. No plumbing. Fixed rather than opening glazing on the QuadPod concept limits ventilation in a room this small. IRISH BUYERS: UK supplier, GBP pricing, no published route to the Republic of Ireland.

THE USE QUESTION COULD MATTER MORE THAN THE MISSING DIMENSIONS. If any model in this collection is intended as living accommodation, the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance is not the applicable test at all — habitable use falls outside Class 3 regardless of area, and the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling route (32-45 m2, rear siting, linked services, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030) would apply instead, with a materially heavier process. Atlas cannot establish which. SECOND, THE COLLECTION STRUCTURE: no footprint, no height, no per-model data, and the same category URL as the supplier's other two records. THIRD, no specification, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: settle the intended use in writing before discussing size or price.

NEITHER STATUTORY TEST CAN BE RUN: no footprint against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, no height against the 3 m and 4 m Class 3 limits. Whatever model is finally chosen will have to be tested on its own dimensions. SECOND, THE THREE-COLLECTION PROBLEM: Studio, Abode and Luxuriance carry identical evidence positions and share one category URL, so a homeowner cannot rank them and any comparison offered between them would be empty. Recorded once as a catalogue limitation for this supplier; not corrected, architecture frozen. THIRD, no specification, warranty or price is held for any of them. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat all three as a single unresolved enquiry until Quinn Offsite differentiates them with model lists and dimensions.

NEITHER STATUTORY TEST CAN BE RUN, AND THE TEST WOULD IN ANY CASE HAVE TO BE APPLIED PER MODEL. With no footprint the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be checked, and with no height the 3 m and 4 m Class 3 limits cannot be checked either. SECOND, THE COLLECTION STRUCTURE IS THE DEFECT: a record standing for several buildings cannot carry product-level intelligence and should not appear in a size, price or performance ranking. Recorded once for this supplier; not corrected, architecture frozen. THIRD, ALL THREE QUINN OFFSITE RECORDS POINT AT THE SAME CATEGORY URL, so nothing distinguishes them in Atlas and evidence neutrality has been preserved between them. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the constituent models before anything else.

AT EUR 15,664 THIS IS AMONG THE MOST EXPENSIVE PRODUCTS IN THE RANGE AND IT ARRIVES WITHOUT INSULATION — which a buyer at that price would reasonably assume was included. Gardenhouse24 sells insulation exclusively as a paid package. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: price the insulation packages and confirm the door specification before comparing this against anything.

THE ATTRIBUTION PROBLEM COMES FIRST. The certified AM-001 layer records that Rayco Modular Homes exists as TWO Organisation records in Atlas — a truth record and a duplicate — unresolved across nine sessions, and that product attribution should be confirmed before this record is surfaced. Duplicates are not merged under the frozen architecture, so the caution stands. THIRD, NOTHING IS MEASURABLE: no footprint and no height, so neither the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance nor the 3 m and 4 m height conditions could be tested. Ex-VAT self-assembly kit. Excludes foundation or base, water and sewerage, electrical installation and HVAC — budget all four separately. Assembly not included. Price EXCLUDES VAT, and excludes foundation or base, water supply and sewerage, electrical installation and HVAC. Ex-VAT self-assembly kit excluding foundation, water and sewerage, electrical installation and HVAC. At 24.8m² self-assembly is a serious project — factor in trade labour honestly. Value per m² is slightly worse than ALOE (EUR 514 vs EUR 480), so compare the two directly. Cross-border supply from Vilnius; bespoke builds 6-10 weeks. Confirm the footprint against Irish exempted-development limits before ordering.

THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK SIZE BAND IN THE CATALOGUE. Zero margin means the exemption survives only on a completely clear plot, and the combined allowance counts every structure in the garden. SECOND, 'TWIN SKIN' IS NOT INSULATION: Quick-Garden's own taxonomy lists 'Twin Skin 44+44 mm' and 'Insulated, Twin Skin 44+44 mm' as SEPARATE specifications, and this record does not say which — the difference is a heated room versus a thicker shell. THIRD, the insulation build-up Atlas holds for this model was INHERITED FROM THE 3 × 6 m SIBLING, not read from this product's own table. FOURTH, Republic of Ireland delivery is unconfirmed and prices are GBP only. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the SKU, the insulation and the delivered Irish price before anything else.

THE ATLAS EVIDENCE ON THIS PRODUCT IS NOT ENTIRELY OF ONE VOICE, AND A BUYER SHOULD KNOW IT. An earlier certified insulation record states a verified build-up with 25 mm insulation on all three planes; the later certified Thermal Usability layer records that a 'TWIN SKIN' designation alone does not establish insulation, because the supplier lists twin-skin walls in BOTH uninsulated and insulated classes. BOTH POSITIONS ARE CERTIFIED AND NEITHER IS REOPENED HERE. SECOND, THE INTERNAL DIMENSIONS ARE PUBLISHED IN THE OPPOSITE ORDER to the external ones, recorded as published rather than reordered. THIRD, 25 mm is a modest insulation layer with no U-value. FOURTH, twin-skin construction increases self-build effort materially, and Irish delivery is unconfirmed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the SKU and the wall class confirmed in writing — that single answer settles it.

IT IS PUBLISHED WITH IDENTICAL SPECIFICATIONS TO THE MIAMI 2.0 ON EVERY MEASURED FIELD — same 28 mm walls, same 292 × 292 cm envelope, same 8.2 m2 floor, same ridge, wall height, overhang, roof area, roof angle and door size. The only difference in the two specification tables is the PALLET WEIGHT, 480 kg against 468 kg. Atlas holds them as two products; on the manufacturer's own evidence they are the same building under two names, and seeing both in a comparison would give a false sense of choice. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat Sacramento and Miami 2.0 as one option, and price the flooring in.

PLANNING PERMISSION IS THE CONSIDERATION, AND THE MEASUREMENT BASIS DECIDES HOW FAR OVER YOU ARE. On the published designation the product is 1.20 m2 above the 30 m2 combined allowance. The certified AM-001 layer records that Shanette does not state whether 5.2 m × 6 m is external or internal: if EXTERNAL, 31.20 m2 is the figure planning uses and the product is over; if INTERNAL, the external footprint is larger still and the overrun widens. There is no reading on which it comes in under the limit. SECOND, THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE MAKES IT WORSE: any existing structure adds to the total. THIRD, THE ONLY URL HELD IS RANGE-LEVEL, so the record is Tier B and no product specification could be attributed. FOURTH, NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: budget for a planning application and a designer, or ask Shanette whether a smaller unit in the same range will meet the brief.

THE MARGIN IS SMALLER THAN THE NUMBER LOOKS. 24.80 m2 leaves about 5.20 m2 of the 30 m2 combined allowance for EVERY other structure on the plot — one ordinary garden shed consumes most of that, and the plot would then exceed the limit even though this building on its own does not. SECOND, THE FIGURE IS A NOMINAL DESIGNATION, NOT A MEASURED FOOTPRINT: the certified AM-001 layer classifies it VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE and warns that a homeowner close to the limit cannot rely on it; Shanette publishes no internal area and no conversion rule. THIRD, THE ONLY URL HELD IS A RANGE-LEVEL PAGE rather than a product page, so no product-specific specification could be attributed and the record is Tier B. FOURTH, NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so the 3 m limit for a flat or non-tiled roof — 4 m only for tiled or slated — cannot be checked. FIFTH, A GYM-SPECIFIC POINT ATLAS CANNOT ANSWER: floor construction and loading for dropped weights. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for a dimensioned plan, the roof height and covering, and the floor build-up.

THE HEIGHT ADVANTAGE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON THE ROOF COVERING, AND THE COVERING IS NOT PUBLISHED. Only a TILED OR SLATED pitched roof attracts the 4 m limit; a pitched roof finished in felt, membrane or metal remains on 3 m. A homeowner assuming 'pitched means 4 m' can be wrong by a full metre. SECOND, THIS IS A RANGE-LEVEL RECORD: no single footprint or height exists, and both tests must be applied to the specific model built. THIRD, nothing else is published either — no area, no U-value, no warranty, no price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the exact roof covering as well as the overall height and footprint for your chosen model, in writing, before ordering.

A RANGE-LEVEL RECORD CANNOT CARRY A PLANNING ANSWER, AND THAT IS THE CENTRAL CAUTION HERE. Different models in one range will have different footprints and different heights, so the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m or 4 m height limits have to be applied to the specific model and specification chosen — never to the range. THE CERTIFIED LAYERS RECORD THIS AS A STRUCTURAL LIMITATION of the record rather than a supplier failing. SECOND, nothing is published at either level: no area, no dimensions, no height. THIRD, no U-value, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not treat any planning statement about the range as applying to your build — get the external footprint and overall height for YOUR model in writing and test that against the combined 30 m2.

CINEMA DESIGN PUSHES A BUILDING UPWARD, AND THAT IS WHERE THE EXEMPTION IS LOST. The certified record makes the point precisely: acoustic treatment and a raised or tiered floor eat into internal height, which pushes designers toward a taller build — and the 3 m flat-roof limit is the tighter of the two height conditions. A homeowner can satisfy themselves on 30 m2 and still breach on height. SECOND, NEITHER FIGURE IS PUBLISHED, so neither test can be run from Atlas evidence. THIRD, no acoustic specification, U-value, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the OVERALL height above finished ground level — not the internal ceiling height — together with the footprint and the roof covering, since a tiled pitched roof buys a 4 m limit instead of 3 m.

THIS IS THE PRODUCT MOST LIKELY IN THE WHOLE CATALOGUE TO BREACH THE HEIGHT LIMIT WHILE PASSING THE AREA TEST. Swing clearance plus screen and projector plus floor build-up plus roof structure is a stack that pushes overall height toward and past 3 m — and only a TILED OR SLATED PITCHED ROOF buys the higher 4 m limit, which is a roof-covering decision as much as a height one. NEITHER HEIGHT NOR FOOTPRINT IS PUBLISHED. SECOND, the certified layers separately note that Atlas carries another golf-use record with the same gap, so the omission is a pattern rather than an oversight. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get internal clear height, overall height above finished ground level, roof covering and footprint in writing — and ask what roof would keep you inside the exemption.

THE FEATURES THAT MAKE IT WORK ARE THE FEATURES THAT THREATEN THE EXEMPTION. Standing cycling clearance sets a minimum internal clear height; a ventilation void sits above that; a floor build-up sits below it — and the overall height above finished ground level is what the 3 m flat-roof limit measures. The certified record records this as a realistic risk, not a theoretical one. NEITHER THE HEIGHT NOR THE FOOTPRINT IS PUBLISHED, so neither statutory test can be run. SECOND, no ventilation or thermal specification, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for internal clear height, overall height above ground level, roof covering and footprint together — and note that a tiled or slated pitched roof raises the limit to 4 m.

SELF-ASSEMBLY MOVES THE COMPLIANCE RESPONSIBILITY ONTO THE BUYER. Siting behind the front wall of the house, keeping 25 m2 of private open space, and the finished HEIGHT above ground level are all decided by how and where the kit is erected — and on a self-built structure there is no installer to get those wrong or right on your behalf. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so neither test can be run from the catalogue. THIRD, base preparation is usually the buyer's responsibility on a kit and can raise the finished height. Poor value per m2 against its siblings: roughly EUR 573/m2, nearly double the Allen at EUR 291/m2 and the Meelagh at EUR 311/m2, both of which have THICKER 80mm walls and far more space. THE PUBLISHED ROOM SCHEDULE CONTAINS AN ERROR: Kitchen & Lounge is listed as 1.5m x 2.5m, identical to the bathroom and implausible for a 42m2 two-bedroom cabin. Get the real layout confirmed before ordering. 42m2 is the external footprint. Services are chargeable extras (EUR 4,800-18,900 on the supplier's guide). VAT status not stated. Assume full planning permission at this size with bedrooms.

IT IS SMALL, AND 2.44 m DEEP IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS. A room under two and a half metres deep takes a desk against one wall and little else; the 10.42 m2 headline flatters the usable layout. Anyone imagining an office plus gym should look further up the range. The value case is weak and should be tested with the supplier. VAT status not stated.

44mm walls with twelve windows is a difficult combination for winter heat retention — lots of glazing and the thinnest wall specification in the range. Budget for the supplier's thicker-wall customisation if this will be a year-round office. The 25 m2 figure is the external footprint (5.0 x 5.0), not verified internal area. No bathroom in the plan. Electrics and plumbing are chargeable add-ons. VAT status not stated. The 3.6m ridge is high enough to warrant checking against Irish exempted-development limits for your site.

A 10m x 10m two-bedroom dwelling — full planning permission should be assumed, and water, drainage and power are all separate projects. The footprint needs a large, accessible site: this is a substantial flatpack to deliver and erect. Shows 'Home Delivery' rather than 'Free Home Delivery' — confirm whether delivery is charged. 100m2 is the external footprint, not verified internal area. A DEFECT THAT REPEATS ACROSS A PRODUCT LINE IS A SUPPLIER PRACTICE, NOT AN ACCIDENT — and that is the useful thing to know here. Because both Nova pavilions carry the same contradictory unit, a homeowner cannot resolve one by reference to the other, and no figure from this line should be relied on without written confirmation. FOURTH, the allowance is COMBINED, so even the favourable reading assumes an otherwise empty garden. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: written confirmation of the external footprint in metres is the first step.

AN UNRESOLVED UNIT IS WORSE THAN NO FIGURE AT ALL, BECAUSE IT INVITES A GUESS. A homeowner who reads '21.5m' as 21.5 m2 will conclude they have 8.5 m2 of headroom; if the figure means something else, that conclusion is unfounded — and the certified layers refused to make the assumption for exactly that reason. THIRD, on a glazed sun room, the absence of any glazing or thermal specification leaves both winter heat loss and summer overheating unassessed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in metres, in writing, before anything else.

44mm walls on a 48m2 two-bedroom cabin — thinner than the 70mm on the far smaller Bofin, and the single biggest reason this model is so cheap. For year-round or residential use the thicker-wall upgrade is close to essential, and its cost is not published. 48m2 is the external footprint, not verified internal area. At this size and with bedrooms, assume full planning permission rather than exempted development. Kitchen, bathroom, plumbing, heating and mains connection are all chargeable extras totalling EUR 4,800-18,900 on the supplier's own guide. VAT status not stated.

TAXONOMY CONFLICT: the supplier's own copy calls this a three-bedroom cabin, yet it is listed under the Two Bed Cabins category. Shows 'Home Delivery' not 'Free Home Delivery'. 120m2 is the external footprint. VAT status not stated.

SEVERE PRICING ANOMALY, VERIFIED AS THE SUPPLIER'S PUBLISHED PRICE. EUR 53,328 for 28.14m2 is about EUR 1,895/m2 against EUR 291/m2 for The Allen (90m2, same 80mm walls) and EUR 304/m2 for the 120m2 three-bedroom Scannal, which costs EUR 16,889 LESS. Services chargeable at EUR 4,800-18,900. VAT status not stated.

THE ONE ROUTE THAT MIGHT WORK CANNOT BE TESTED, BECAUSE NO AREA IS PUBLISHED. Class 3A requires 32–45 m2, rear siting, services linked to the principal house and 14 days' notice — and with no floor area held, a homeowner cannot tell whether this annexe even reaches the 32 m2 floor. A HABITABLE UNIT BELOW THAT THRESHOLD HAS NO FAST ROUTE AT ALL and needs full planning permission. SECOND, a dwelling brings Building Regulations, drainage and services obligations a garden room does not. THIRD, no height, insulation or price is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish the intended use and the confirmed floor area, then put both to your planning authority before ordering.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE PLANNING CLAIM MUST NOT BE RELIED ON IN IRELAND: the supplier describes the Annexe as self-contained living with kitchen and bathroom, 'installable under the CARAVAN ACT with no planning permission'. That is a UK legal route. It does not apply in Ireland, where the position on a habitable garden building is different — the Class 3 back-garden exemption requires incidental use with NO HUMAN HABITATION, and a kitchen-and-bathroom annexe falls outside it on use, whatever its width. Recorded as intelligence; Atlas makes no determination. TWO, AVAILABILITY: free delivery and installation in ENGLAND, GBP 899 to Scotland within 100 miles of Edinburgh or Glasgow, NO IRISH DELIVERY PUBLISHED. Corby, Northamptonshire. THREE, THE GUARANTEE HAS A CONDITION THAT CAN DESTROY IT: Booths-installed bathrooms and kitchens preserve portability AND the guarantee; THIRD-PARTY INSTALLATIONS REDUCE THE GUARANTEE TO ONE YEAR and prevent the building being moved. On an annexe — the one configuration where a buyer might be tempted to use their own plumber — that is the most consequential contractual term this supplier publishes. FOUR, GROUNDWORKS RETURN: a SITE VISIT IS REQUIRED where a bathroom, kitchen or sink is installed, because groundworks are then quoted — so the no-concrete-base advantage weakens on precisely this model. FIVE: HEATING IS NOT INCLUDED (air conditioning roughly GBP 1,700 plus a two-yearly service); NO U-VALUE is published; and an unreconciled inconsistency stands — 90 mm of wall insulation stated alongside a 75 mm panel thickness. No dimensions or area are held: DO NOT RANK.

THE PREMIUM BUILD IS ALSO A RANKING TRAP, AND THE CERTIFIED LAYER SAYS SO EXPLICITLY: ranking this product on its 12 m2 label against UNINSULATED products of the same label would systematically flatter it, because the thicker walls mean less usable floor for the same nominal size. Comparing like with like requires an internal figure Waltons does not publish. SECOND, NO U-VALUE IS PUBLISHED, so the premium claim cannot be quantified — the difference is named but not measured. THIRD, no height, no product URL, no warranty and no price; all Waltons records are Tier B. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what 'premium' means in millimetres and in U-value, and get the internal dimensions.

The 10-year guarantee is anti-rot only and is conditional on treating the timber every year — skip a year and the cover is at risk, so budget the time and cost for the life of the building. The published figure is a Sale Price, not a standard price, so it may not be available when you buy. No U-values are published despite the premium insulation label. Priced in GBP: Irish buyers must confirm delivery to Ireland, installation and currency terms before comparing against euro-priced Irish suppliers.

THE COMBINED FOOTPRINT IS THE FIGURE THAT MATTERS AND IT IS NOT PUBLISHED. A buyer who thinks of the tub as equipment and only counts the sauna will understate what the 30 m2 allowance measures, because the unit occupies one continuous footprint. The certified AM-006 layer makes that explicit and records that the test could not be run. SECOND, NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so the 3 m limit for a non-tiled roof cannot be checked. THIRD, SERVICES ARE HEAVIER THAN FOR EITHER ELEMENT ALONE — electrical supply, water fill and drainage — and none is specified. FOURTH, no warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the overall external footprint of the complete unit and its maximum height, in writing.

THE ONLY PLANNING RISK IS WHAT YOU BUILD AROUND IT. The certified AM-006 layer records that a tub is not a habitable structure, but if it is HOUSED or DECKED it may form part of a garden structure counting toward the combined 30 m2 allowance — a site question the product cannot answer. SECOND, NO SPECIFICATION IS HELD: no dimensions, capacity, chiller or filtration detail, warranty or price, so nothing can be said about running cost or maintenance. THIRD, the vocabulary limitation recorded in the certified layer stands: the classification set assumes an enclosed structure and does not fit a vessel. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: keep it free-standing and the planning question stays closed.

NO FIXED SIZE MEANS NO ADVANCE TEST. The certified AM-006 layer records that the 30 m2 allowance cannot be tested against a product with no fixed area, and that the buyer must obtain the AS-ORDERED footprint before assuming exemption. SECOND, THE BARREL FORM COMPLICATES HEIGHT: a curved roof reaches its maximum at the centre line, and because it is not tiled or slated the tighter 3 m limit applies — ask for the height at the highest point above finished ground level. THIRD, a sauna needs an electrical supply and a level base, neither specified in Atlas. FOURTH, no warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: agree footprint and maximum height in writing before the order is placed.

THE PLANNING POSITION DEPENDS ON THE INSTALLATION, NOT THE PRODUCT. A free-standing tub on an existing patio is not normally a garden structure; a tub that is DECKED, HOUSED, ROOFED or built into an enclosure becomes part of a structure whose footprint counts toward the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. Atlas cannot answer that from the catalogue. SECOND, A WOOD-FIRED UNIT HAS A FLUE, raising siting and neighbour-amenity questions outside the exemption tests. THIRD, no dimensions, warranty or price are held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: describe the whole installation, including any decking, to your planning office — not just the tub.

A 'PLUS' THAT IS NOT DEFINED IS A PRICE PREMIUM WITHOUT A STATED RETURN. Every Tonio record in this catalogue carries the suffix, and nothing published says what it delivers — so a buyer cannot tell whether they are paying for size, insulation, glazing or fittings. SECOND, IF 'PLUS' MEANS A LARGER BUILDING, it also means a larger claim on the combined 30 m2 allowance, and no audited area exists to check. THIRD, no height or roof form, so the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: make the supplier itemise what 'Plus' includes.

TWO UNDEFINED MODIFIERS ON THE LARGER MODEL IS THE WORST POSITION IN THE LINE. If the numeral means size and the Plus means more, this is the Tonio nearest both the 30 m2 combined allowance and the height limit — and neither meaning is established, nor is any figure held. SECOND, NO ROOF FORM IS RECORDED, so a homeowner cannot even tell whether 3 m or 4 m applies. THIRD, Estonia-only shipping with no distributor to resolve a problem after delivery. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on the larger model of an undescribed line, ask for a dimensioned drawing rather than a description.

JURISDICTION FIRST, AS WITH THE WHOLE RANGE: a Northern Ireland supplier operating under the UK permitted-development regime at its own location, while the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m and 4 m height limits apply only to a Republic of Ireland site. Confirm the rules of the jurisdiction your SITE is in. SECOND, NEITHER STATUTORY TEST CAN BE RUN because no footprint and no height are published, and no product URL is held, so the record is Tier B throughout. THIRD, AND SPECIFIC TO THIS RECORD, THE TWO MODELS ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE IN ATLAS: The Lagan and The Sperrin carry identical evidence positions, which means neither can be ranked against the other, and a comparison presented to a homeowner would be empty. Recorded once as a catalogue limitation; not corrected, architecture frozen. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat both models as a single unresolved enquiry until the supplier differentiates them.

JURISDICTION IS THE CONSIDERATION MOST LIKELY TO BE GOT WRONG. The supplier is based in Northern Ireland, where the Irish exempted-development regime does not apply — Northern Ireland has its own permitted development rules. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, the 25 m2 private open space condition and the 3 m and 4 m height limits recorded in the certified AM-006 layer govern a REPUBLIC OF IRELAND site only. Planning guidance offered by a supplier from its own jurisdiction should not be applied to a Republic address without checking, and cross-border buyers are the group most exposed to this in either direction. SECOND, NOTHING IS MEASURABLE: no area, no dimensions, no height and no product URL, so the record is Tier B throughout and cannot be tested under either regime. THIRD, NO PRICE OR SPECIFICATION IS HELD. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: check the rules of the jurisdiction your SITE is in, not your supplier's.

IT FAILS EVERY EXEMPT ROUTE ON TWO INDEPENDENT GROUNDS EACH, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE CONSIDERATION. On area, 48.28 m2 exceeds both the 30 m2 Class 3 allowance and the 45 m2 Class 3A ceiling. On use, a two-bedroom residential cabin is habitation, which Class 3 excludes at any size. THE UNSTATED MEASUREMENT BASIS CANNOT HELP, because the published figure already exceeds every threshold. SECOND, a dwelling of this scale brings Building Regulations, drainage, services and fire and access considerations. THIRD, the certified layers record the category placement issue once; recorded, not corrected. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: budget for drawings, fees and a planning timeline, and do not treat the Garden Rooms category label as any guide to the regulatory position.

Considerations from published evidence: the 45.87 m2 footprint is 153% of the statutory allowance and also sits above the Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling range; 23.87 m2 of the footprint is unexplained by the title; the division of the 22 m2 between the two rooms is not published; only 48% of the ground covered is published room area; no insulation specification is published; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

Considerations from published evidence: the division of the 21 m2 between the two rooms is not published, so neither room's size can be established before ordering; 5.64 m2 of the footprint is unexplained by the title; the 26.64 m2 footprint leaves only 3.36 m2 of the statutory allowance; no insulation or heating specification is published; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

THE ATTRIBUTION QUESTION COMES BEFORE EVERY OTHER QUESTION, AND IT IS UNRESOLVED. The certified AM-001 layer records this as the only Garden Room product in Atlas with NO ORGANISATION LINK, and states plainly that it cannot be attributed to a supplier in its present state. The certified AM-006 layer added a cross-layer note, recorded once: the Products table now shows an organisation link to 'Garden Rooms' which the AM-001 record does not reflect, and the attribution remains to be reconciled.
