THIRD, THE RECORD IS RANGE-LEVEL rather than a product, so it could not carry product-level intelligence even if a supplier were confirmed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: there is no company to contact and no building to price.

At 9.83m2 internal this is a compact studio — comfortably a one-person office, but tight as a gym or for two people working side by side. GBP 19,195 is high per square metre against larger rooms in the same price band, so the premium buys specification and thermal performance rather than floor space. Priced in GBP: Irish buyers should confirm delivery to this island, currency and installation terms before comparing directly against euro-priced Irish suppliers.

GBP 15,995 for a 2.4m x 2.4m nominal building is the highest price per square metre in the Sanctum range — the premium buys maintenance-free cladding and specification, not floor space. Internal dimensions are 0.15m smaller than the nominal name on each axis. Sanctum requires 35cm clearance around the studio to fit the cladding, which matters in a tight garden; weatherboard can be substituted to sit closer to a boundary. The published U-values are approximate and self-declared, with no test standard or certifying body cited. No plumbing offered; the only insulation upgrade is acoustic and does not improve thermal performance. IRISH BUYERS: UK supplier, GBP pricing, no published delivery route to the Republic of Ireland, and UK-only planning guidance.

A PRODUCT MARKETED FOR FAMILY USE INVITES EXACTLY THE USE THE EXEMPTION FORBIDS. Sleeping accommodation is habitation, and habitation removes the Class 3 exemption at any floor area — so a homeowner attracted by the family framing can end up needing full planning permission for a building they assumed was exempt. IF THE INTENDED USE IS GENUINELY OVERNIGHT, the Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route is the relevant one, and it carries a MINIMUM of 32 m2, rear siting, linked services and 14 days' notice. SECOND, no area, dimensions or height are published, so neither the 30 m2 allowance nor the height limits can be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: put the intended use in writing to your planning authority before ordering.

THE AVAILABILITY QUESTION COMES BEFORE EVERY OTHER QUESTION. vilarte.be is a Belgian domain and Atlas holds no evidence of an Irish purchasing, delivery or installation route. Until that is settled, price, specification and planning are all academic. SECOND, NOTHING IS MEASURABLE: no footprint, no height and no floor area are published, so the certified AM-006 layer could not run the 30 m2 combined back-garden test against this product. THIRD, A PAVILION FORM RAISES A TRAP: if the structure is roofed but open-sided, the roofed footprint still counts in full toward the 30 m2 allowance — an open pavilion is not free of the area test. FOURTH, no price is held, so no value comparison is possible. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat this as an enquiry, not a shortlist entry.

THREE METRES OF DEPTH IS UNDER FOUR ONCE THE WALLS ARE COUNTED, and on a log building that is not a small deduction. What remains is a single-aspect room: a desk wall, a walkway, and no space opposite. SECOND, NO WALL CLASS IS HELD — the model name carries no construction information, and Quick-Garden publishes eleven distinct specifications from a plain 28 mm log to 'Insulated, SIPS'. THIRD, the advertised figure is a kit price with installation separately quoted and the base extra. FOURTH, Republic of Ireland delivery is unconfirmed and prices are GBP only. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the internal width, not the external one.

THE USE CONDITION APPLIES EVEN WITHOUT A CRAFT IN THE NAME. A general workshop that becomes a place where paid work is done is business use, and business use may fall outside the Class 3 exemption at any floor area — the caution the certified layers attach to all five workshop records. SECOND, THE NUMERAL ESTABLISHES NOTHING, and no audited area is held, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested. THIRD, no height, so the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be either. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: keep the use domestic, and get the footprint in writing.

A BIGGER WORKSHOP IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BECOME A BUSINESS PREMISES, and that is the risk the certified layers single out for this category. Space invites commissions; commissions are paid work; and paid work is not use incidental to the enjoyment of the house, which removes the exemption at any floor area. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD, and the 30 m2 is COMBINED across every garden structure. THIRD, no height, so the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the workshop might ever earn money, settle the planning position before it does.

THE LARGEST WORKSHOP IS THE MOST EXPOSED ON EVERY CONDITION AT ONCE. On USE, a big workshop is the likeliest to host paid work, which the certified record warns may take it outside the exemption entirely. On AREA, the 30 m2 is COMBINED across every back-garden structure and no audited figure exists. On HEIGHT, machinery and material storage push toward taller buildings, and no height is published. AND ON AVAILABILITY, Estonia-only shipping means no supplier on the ground if any of these becomes a problem after delivery. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: settle use, footprint and height in writing — and the purchasing route before any of them.

THE USE CONDITION CAN DEFEAT THIS PRODUCT BEFORE ANY MEASUREMENT IS TAKEN. A workshop where furniture is made for sale is a business use, not use incidental to the enjoyment of a house, and the certified record warns that it may fall outside the exemption entirely — regardless of how small the building is. SECOND, WORKSHOPS GENERATE NOISE AND DUST, which raises neighbour questions the exemption tests do not address. THIRD, no audited area or height is held, so neither statutory test can be run. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if any of the work is paid, put it to your planning authority before ordering.

TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS SIT ON THIS RECORD, AND THE CATALOGUE ANSWERS NEITHER. FIRST, USE: a smithy operated as a business falls outside the incidental-use condition and therefore outside the exemption at any size, as the certified record warns for all five workshops. SECOND, SAFETY AND SPECIFICATION: hot work in a timber garden building raises fire, ventilation and insurance questions that no published detail addresses — no materials, no lining, no ventilation figure. THIRD, no audited area or height. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish what the building is lined and ventilated with before assuming it suits hot work.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. Both certified and frozen; flagged for the Layer Completion Audit.

TWO MARGINS ARE THIN AT ONCE, AND BOTH SHOULD BE CHECKED BEFORE ORDERING. ON AREA: 26.04 m2 leaves under 4 m2 of the 30 m2 combined allowance, so a plot with any existing shed or garage will very likely exceed the limit once this is added — and on the footprint it would have been over the pre-2026 limit outright. A buyer who checks the 24 m2 living-space figure against the allowance instead of the footprint will reach the wrong answer, which is exactly the error the separate publication of both figures exists to prevent. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: total the garden, and get the finished height above ground level in writing.

THE HEADLINE FIGURE IS THE INTERNAL ONE, AND THAT MATTERS FOR GROUNDWORKS. The certified AM-001 layer records that the marketing copy quotes 'measuring 5m x 3m' — the LIVING SPACE — while the base and the garden position must be set out from the 5.2 × 3.2 m footprint. Two hundred millimetres in each direction is enough to build a base the wrong size. SECOND, IT CONSUMES OVER HALF THE ALLOWANCE: 16.64 m2 leaves about 13.4 m2 of the combined 30 m2 for every other structure, so an existing garage needs measuring before ordering. THIRD, NO CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATION, INSULATION VALUE, WARRANTY TERM OR PRICE IS HELD in Atlas, so this record cannot answer questions about winter comfort or value — only about size and compliance. FOURTH, JURISDICTION: a Co. Down supplier serving both markets; confirm which regime governs your site. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: build to 5.2 × 3.2 m, not 5 × 3 m.

THE ONE TRAP IS IN THE MARKETING COPY, NOT THE DATA. The certified AM-001 layer records that Yardbox's own page calls this 'our most compact garden room measuring 3M x 3M' — but that 3 m × 3 m is the INTERNAL dimension, not the footprint. A homeowner working from the headline will under-size their base by 200 mm in each direction. The correct figure for groundworks and for the planning test is 3.2 m × 3.2 m. SECOND, IT IS GENUINELY SMALL: 9 m2 usable is one desk, one chair and a little storage — a single-function room. THIRD, NO CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATION, INSULATION VALUE, WARRANTY TERM OR PRICE IS HELD in Atlas, so year-round comfort and value cannot be assessed from this record. FOURTH, JURISDICTION: a Co. Down base serving both markets, so confirm which planning regime applies to your site. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: set your base out from 3.2 m, not 3 m.

NOTHING MEASURABLE IS PUBLISHED, SO NO PLANNING TEST CAN BE RUN. With no footprint the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be checked, and with no height neither the 3 m flat-roof nor the 4 m pitched limit can be. THE LONGER FORM IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO APPROACH THE AREA LIMIT, which makes the omission most consequential here. SECOND, USE MATTERS AS MUCH AS SIZE: if the unit is used for sleeping or guest accommodation it falls outside the Class 3 exemption at any area, and mirror-glass units are commonly bought for exactly that. THIRD, ÖÖD is an Estonian manufacturer with no published Irish purchasing route, so siting, delivery and compliance would rest with the buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get external footprint and overall height in writing, and be clear about intended use.

THE EXEMPTION IS UNAVAILABLE BEFORE SIZE IS EVEN CONSIDERED. Overnight habitation and commercial letting each independently take this product outside Class 3, so obtaining the footprint would not rescue it — and no footprint, dimension or height is published in any case. A SECOND LAYER APPLIES TO ANY OPERATOR: short-term letting brings its own registration, fire safety, insurance and change-of-use obligations that have nothing to do with garden-structure rules. THIRD, ÖÖD is an Estonian manufacturer with no published Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you are buying this for a domestic garden, you are almost certainly buying the wrong product; if you are buying it as an operator, the planning route is a full application.

THREE PROBLEMS STACK ON THIS PRODUCT. FIRST, PRIVACY: heavy glazing in a suburban back garden raises overlooking questions with neighbours that no exemption test addresses, and which can surface after the building is up. SECOND, THE USUAL RANGE GAPS: no published footprint or height, so neither the 30 m2 allowance nor the 3 m limit can be tested. THIRD, THERMAL PERFORMANCE IS UNQUANTIFIED on the product where it matters most — a largely glass building without a published U-value or solar-control specification is an unknown in both an Irish winter and a warm afternoon. FOURTH, no Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: discuss the siting with neighbours and the planning office before ordering, and ask specifically about glazing specification and overheating.

THE MOST IMPORTANT WARNING IS THE ONE THE CERTIFIED LAYER STATES DIRECTLY: DO NOT ASSUME THAT BECAUSE A UNIT IS DESCRIBED AS MOBILE IT ESCAPES PLANNING CONTROL — and equally, do not assume it is caught by the garden-structure rules either. Which regime applies depends on how the unit is sited, and that could not be resolved from published evidence. SECOND, the range's standard gaps apply: no area, no dimensions, no height, no product URL. THIRD, no published Irish purchasing route from an Estonian manufacturer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: put this specific product, with its method of siting, to your local authority planning office — and obtain external footprint, overall height and siting method from ÖÖD in writing first.

HEIGHT IS THE UNDER-CHECKED TEST, AND THIS IS THE PRODUCT THAT PROVES IT. A homeowner who satisfies themselves on 30 m2 may still lose the exemption on the 3 m flat-roof limit — and the certified layers record that this is a realistic risk for tall, narrow mirror-glass forms. NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so it cannot be tested. SECOND, the same total absence of area and dimensions applies here as across the range. THIRD, sleeping or guest use removes the exemption regardless of size. FOURTH, no published Irish purchasing route from an Estonian manufacturer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: put the height question first with this product, and get the answer measured from finished ground level to the highest point.

THE NAMING CLASH IS A PRACTICAL RISK, NOT A TRIVIA POINT. Because Luxury Garden Studios also markets a 'Signature' range, a homeowner can assemble a specification from the wrong supplier's page and take it to a planning check — and since ÖÖD publishes no figures of its own, there is nothing to contradict the mistake. SECOND, THE STANDARD RANGE GAPS APPLY: no footprint and no height, so neither the 30 m2 allowance nor the 3 m limit can be tested. THIRD, sleeping or guest use removes the exemption at any size. FOURTH, no published Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: source every figure directly from ÖÖD in writing, and check the letterhead before you rely on it.

A PRODUCT NAMED FOR ITS SIZE THAT PUBLISHES NO SIZE IS THE WORST COMBINATION FOR AN EXEMPTION CHECK. The 30 m2 allowance is COMBINED across every structure already in the back garden, so a large unit can breach it even on an empty-looking site, and there is no published footprint to test. NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED EITHER, and the certified layers note that mirror-glass units tend to be tall for their footprint — the 3 m flat-roof limit may bind before the area limit does. THIRD, sleeping or guest use removes the exemption at any size. FOURTH, no Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain external footprint and overall height above finished ground level in writing, and add the footprint to every existing shed and store before assuming 30 m2 is intact.
